body:
WHAT
Token pricing is modelled with four separate rates per model (input, output, cache read, cache write) in dollars per million tokens, because the four token classes bill differently. A model that has no entry in the built-in table or in the user's settings.pricing has no rate card at all: pricingFor returns undefined, and the engine never shows an invented $0.00. The /session report and the model hint currently show token counts only and omit any dollar figure.

WHY
Collapsing the classes into 'in/out' misprices cached conversations badly, and a fabricated $0.00 for an unpriced model would look like a real (free) bill.

WHERE
engine/core/src/config/pricing.ts — interface ModelPricing {input, output, cacheRead?, cacheWrite?}, MODEL_PRICING table, pricingFor(model, settings) (settings.pricing wins, else table, else undefined). engine/core/src/runtime/sessionStats.ts — SessionStats.format() (cost deliberately omitted; per-model usage printed as four separate classes), SessionStats.byModel. engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — buildRateCard() ships the four rates plus contextWindow per model in session_started (only for models where pricingFor is defined).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. pricingFor('no-such-model') with no settings returns undefined; pricingFor('zai-org/GLM-5') returns the table entry with input 0.6 and output 2.08.
2. pricingFor(model, {pricing:{[model]:{input:1, output:2}}}) returns the settings entry even when the built-in table also has that model (user override wins).
3. buildRateCard(settings) omits models with no pricing and, for a priced model, includes cacheRead/cacheWrite only when the entry defines them.
4. SessionStats.format() output for a session with recorded usage contains 'input', 'output', 'cache read' and 'cache write' figures per model and contains no '$' character (no cost line, so never a fabricated $0.00).
5. SessionStats.format() for a session with no calls prints '(no model calls yet)' and no dollar amount.
